architecture_rationale.claim: Several controllers issue DMA using function 1 as the requester ID even when they are function 0; without an alias, the IOMMU blocks that DMA.

evidence.excerpt: they use function 1 as the PCIe requester ID

intentional_vs_accidental.claim: Function 1 may not even exist on some SKUs (a 'ghost requester'); the alias is added regardless.

evidence.excerpt: in other SKUs this function is not present, making this a ghost requester.

hardware_timing_dependencies.claim: Only matters when an IOMMU is active (VT-d, AMD-Vi, ARM SMMU); without IOMMU the bug is invisible.

evidence.excerpt: Some quick testing with the ARM SMMU enabled reveals that it suffers from the same requester ID mixup problems

suspected_workarounds.claim: Silicon bug in Marvell 88SE91xx/92xx family; tracked in one long-running bugzilla (42679) since 2012.

external_interfaces.claim: Output consumed by IOMMU drivers via the device's DMA alias list.

compatibility_certification_sensitive.claim: Removing an entry makes the disk controller fail to initialise under IOMMU.

evidence.excerpt: Without this patch, device initialization fails with DMA errors

reasoning.claim: Storage controller becomes unusable (no disks) whenever IOMMU is enabled - which is exactly the configuration security-hardened systems use.

evidence.excerpt: the same DMA requester ID hardware bug that prevents it from working under IOMMU
